diagnosis_explanation: Your baby was ready to be born. You had a cesarean birth. This is a surgery to deliver your baby. You also had a surgery to prevent future pregnancies. This is called sterilization.
medication_rationale:
Vitamins:
This medicine gives you the nutrients your body needs.
It helps keep you and your baby healthy.
You should not notice any changes.
Call your doctor if you feel sick to your stomach.

Iron:
This medicine helps your body make red blood cells.
It helps prevent anemia, which is low iron.
You may notice your stools are dark or black. This is normal.
Call your doctor if you get bad stomach pain.

Motrin:
This medicine helps with pain after your surgery.
It can also help lower a fever.
You may feel less pain. Your body may feel more comfortable.
Call your doctor if you get a rash.
Also call if your stomach hurts a lot.

Percocet:
This medicine helps manage pain after your surgery.
You may feel less pain. It helps you rest.
You might feel sleepy or dizzy. This is normal.
Call your doctor if you feel very confused.
Also call if you have trouble breathing.
Call 911 right away if you have sudden face drooping, arm weakness, or trouble speaking.

Paxil:
This medicine helps with feelings of sadness or worry.
It can help improve your mood.
You might feel sleepy at first. This is often temporary.
Call your doctor if you have thoughts of hurting yourself.
Call your doctor if your mood gets worse.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will feel tired and sore after surgery. This is normal.
- Keep pain under control with the medicine your doctor gave you.
- Do not lift anything heavier than your baby.
- Do not strain or push hard.
- Do not drive a car.
- Do not put anything inside your vagina.
- Your goal is to rest and heal.
- Call your doctor if you have severe pain.

**Week 2:**
- You may feel a little less tired this week.
- Keep up with your pain medicine as needed.
- You can walk around your home more.
- Do not lift anything heavier than your baby.
- Do not strain or push hard.
- Do not drive a car.
- Do not put anything inside your vagina.
- Your goal is to walk a little further each day.

**Week 3:**
- You should start to feel more energy each day.
- You can do light activities around the house.
- Do not lift anything heavier than your baby.
- Do not strain or push hard.
- Do not drive a car.
- Do not put anything inside your vagina.
- Your goal is to walk for 10 minutes outside.
- Call your doctor if you have heavy bleeding.

**Week 4:**
- Your pain should continue to get better.
- You can do more daily tasks.
- Do not lift anything heavier than your baby.
- Do not strain or push hard.
- Ask your doctor before driving.
- Do not put anything inside your vagina.
- Your goal is to walk for 15 minutes each day.
- Call your doctor if you get a fever.

**Week 5:**
- You will likely feel much stronger now.
- You can return to most light activities.
- Do not lift anything heavier than your baby.
- Do not strain or push hard.
- You may drive if your doctor says it is okay.
- Do not put anything inside your vagina.
- Your goal is to walk for 20 minutes each day.
- Call your doctor if you have other problems.

**Week 6:**
- Most discomfort should be gone by now.
- You can do more household chores.
- Discuss lifting and exercise with your doctor.
- You may drive as needed.
- Do not put anything inside your vagina until your doctor says it is safe.
- Your goal is to return to your normal routine slowly.
- Call your doctor if you have severe pain or heavy bleeding.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Healing takes time, be patient with yourself.
- Follow all activity and lifting rules.
- Call your doctor with any concerns.
- You should feel much better in about 6 to 8 weeks.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Severe pain: This is not normal after surgery.
- Heavy bleeding: Soak a pad in one hour.
- Fever: Your temperature is over 100.4 F.
- Other problems: You feel very sick now.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Pain not helped by medicine: Take Motrin or Percocet.
- Bleeding that soaks a pad hourly: Use pads and count.
- Fever above 101 F: You may have an infection.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Mild pain improving slowly: Motrin should help you heal.
- Questions about your medicine: Your nurse can help you plan.
